chunks: And in another Hadith, he said: 'I said, "What is the limit of humility such that when the servant practices it, he becomes humble?"'

So he said: 'Humility has levels; among them is that a person recognizes his own worth and places it in its proper station with a sound heart, not loving to go to anyone except with the same as he loves to be brought to him.'
If he sees a fault, he covers it with a good deed, the one who swallows his anger, who pardons people. And Allah loves the good-doers.'

key_terms.التَّوَاضُع: Humility; the quality of being humble and modest
key_terms.دَرَأَهَا بِالْحَسَنَةِ: He covers/averts the fault with a good deed
key_terms.قَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ: A sound/healthy heart; free from hypocrisy and arrogance
key_terms.كَاظِمُ الْغَيْظِ: The one who swallows/restrains his anger

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and behavioral markers of true humility in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents humility as a dynamic equilibrium of self-knowledge and social reciprocity, where the believer maintains a 'sound heart' by treating others with the same respect they desire. This definition moves beyond mere physical lowliness to encompass active moral virtues like suppressing anger and pardoning faults, reflecting the Shia emphasis on internal spiritual states manifesting in external conduct. The narration concludes by linking these traits to divine favor, reinforcing the concept that ethical perfection is a means of attaining Allah's love.
